questions.question: The distance between two consecutive crests of a wave is its:
questions.explanation: Wavelength is the distance between matching points on a wave, such as crest to crest. Frequency and period relate to time; amplitude is height.
steps: Identify spatial measure along the wave

questions.question: The height of a wave from the midline to a crest is its:
questions.explanation: Amplitude measures wave height from the middle to a crest or trough. Wavelength is horizontal distance; period and frequency are time-related.

questions.question: Frequency is measured in:
questions.explanation: Frequency is cycles per second, measured in hertz (Hz). Joules measure energy, meters length, newtons force.
steps: Other units belong to different quantities

questions.question: Light bending when it enters water from air is called:
questions.explanation: Refraction is the change in direction of a wave when it enters a new medium. Reflection bounces back; diffraction spreads around edges; absorption takes in energy.
steps: Direction change in new medium = refraction
Reflection is bounce, diffraction is spreading

questions.question: A mirror produces which wave behavior?
questions.explanation: Mirrors bounce light back, which is reflection. Refraction bends through materials; diffraction is spreading; absorption takes in light.
steps: Other behaviors involve passing or absorbing

questions.question: Sound travels fastest in:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium and travels fastest in solids like steel because particles are closely packed. It cannot travel in vacuum.
steps: Sound speed highest with strong particle coupling
questions.fastStrategy: Sound: solids fastest, gases slowest, none in vacuum.

questions.question: The color of visible light depends mainly on its:
questions.explanation: Color corresponds to light's frequency (or wavelength). Amplitude affects brightness; speed in vacuum is constant for light.
steps: Speed of light in vacuum constant

questions.question: Which wave is mechanical and needs a medium?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and requires a medium. Light, radio, and X-rays are electromagnetic and can travel through vacuum.
questions.fastStrategy: If it fails in vacuum, it's mechanical (sound).

questions.question: Electromagnetic waves differ from sound waves because EM waves:
questions.explanation: EM waves can travel through vacuum; sound cannot. EM waves are transverse and can be polarized.
steps: Recall EM waves move in vacuum
questions.fastStrategy: EM works in space; sound doesn't.

questions.question: When light reflects, the angle of incidence equals the angle of:
questions.explanation: Law of reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, measured from the normal.
steps: Refraction angle differs in new medium

questions.question: A lens that is thicker at the center than edges is a:
questions.explanation: A convex lens bulges outward, thicker in the middle. Concave is thinner in the middle.

questions.question: Which wave property relates to how loud a sound is perceived?
questions.explanation: Loudness correlates with amplitude of the sound wave. Frequency relates to pitch.

questions.question: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: Light travels about 3.0 × 10^8 meters per second in vacuum.

questions.question: When a wave passes through a narrow opening and spreads out, this is:
questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading of waves when they encounter an opening or obstacle.
steps: Refraction is bending in a new medium

questions.question: Constructive interference occurs when two waves:

choices.B: Add to make a larger amplitude

questions.explanation: Constructive interference is when waves align crest-to-crest, producing a larger amplitude. Destructive interference cancels.
steps: Crest aligns with crest → bigger amplitude

questions.question: Destructive interference makes the resulting wave:
questions.explanation: Destructive interference occurs when crest meets trough, reducing amplitude or canceling the wave.
steps: No color or speed change directly

questions.question: Polarization filters out waves based on:
questions.explanation: Polarization selects waves oscillating in a particular plane (direction of vibration). It doesn't change wavelength or frequency.
steps: Not a speed or wavelength filter
questions.fastStrategy: Polarizers pass one vibration plane only.

questions.question: Which color of visible light has the longest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Within visible light, red has the longest wavelength (lowest frequency), and violet has the shortest.
questions.fastStrategy: Visible spectrum: Red = longest λ, Violet = shortest λ.

questions.question: Which color of visible light has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Violet is at the short-wavelength, high-frequency end of visible light.
steps: Violet is shortest λ, highest f

questions.question: When white light passes through a prism, it spreads into colors because of:
questions.explanation: Dispersion occurs when different wavelengths refract by different amounts, separating colors.

questions.question: A transverse wave vibrates:

choices.A: Parallel to its direction of travel
choices.B: Perpendicular to its direction of travel

questions.explanation: In transverse waves, the disturbance is perpendicular to the direction of propagation. Longitudinal waves vibrate parallel.

questions.question: Sound waves in air are:
questions.explanation: Sound in air is a longitudinal wave: compressions and rarefactions move parallel to propagation.
steps: Pressure varies along direction of travel
questions.fastStrategy: Sound in fluids = longitudinal pressure wave.

questions.question: The time for one full wave cycle is the:
questions.explanation: Period is the time for one complete cycle. Frequency is cycles per second, its inverse.
steps: Define period as time per cycle

questions.question: If a wave's frequency increases, its period:
questions.explanation: Frequency and period are inverses. Higher frequency means shorter period.

questions.question: In the wave equation v = fλ, doubling the wavelength while keeping speed constant will:
questions.explanation: With v constant, v = fλ. If λ doubles, f must halve to keep v the same.
